title: The name may be civil, after Augustine, taken from the heavenly city rather than the earthly
source_text: XII. Quo vero nomine sit honor iste signandus, parum referre existimant; dummodo de re ipsa constet, quibus, scilicet, in rebus ille constituendus sit, & quibus actibus & signis testandus atque exhibendus. Nolunt tamen simpliciter Religiosum dici, quoniam religio solum cultum divinum proprie & directe spectat; sed potius civilem, vel ut loquitur Augustinus, societatis & dilectionis. Non quod eum confundant cum illo cultu quem civilis dignitas, & naturae quaedam praestantia requirit: hunc enim, ut dictum, gradu saltem superat. Sed cum duplex sit civitas, una terrena, & altera caelestis, civilem dici posse putant denominatione sumpta, non a civitate terrena, sed caelesti, ad quam pertinet gratia & gloria, cui cultus & honor ille deferendus est.
pass_a_gloss: But by what name that honor is to be marked they think matters little, provided the thing itself is clear, namely in what matters it is to be constituted, and by what acts and signs it is to be attested and shown. They do not want it called religious simply, since religion properly and directly regards only the divine cult; but rather civil, or, as Augustine speaks, of society and love. Not that they confuse it with that cult which civil dignity and a certain excellence of nature require: for, as was said, it surpasses this at least in degree. But since the city is twofold, one earthly and the other heavenly, they think it can be called civil by a name taken not from the earthly city but from the heavenly, to which grace and glory belong, and to which that cult and honor is to be paid.
pass_b_english: What the honor is called matters less to them than what it consists in and how it is shown.
They refuse the bare name religious, because religion properly looks only to God's cult.
They prefer civil, or Augustine's phrase, a cult of fellowship and love.
Civil here is taken from the heavenly city of grace and glory, and it still outranks earthly civic respect in degree.

choices.why: The thesis subordinates the label to the acts that constitute the honor.
rejected: the name is the whole controversy
